policies.summary: A board of county commissioners may designate all or part of the county's unincorporated area as a restricted area that bars large solar facilities and wind farms of 5 MW or more, and the Power Siting Board may not accept applications there; the county may also prohibit or shrink an individual project within 90 days after the developer's required public meeting.

No political subdivision may require any approval, permit or other condition for a major utility facility or economically significant wind farm holding a Board certificate, apart from local rules unrelated to location, design or pollution control.

The Power Siting Board certificates generating plants of 50 MW or more and wind farms of 5 to 50 MW; county and township zoning governs smaller solar and wind, and counties hold a separate veto under SB 52 (see OH-local_opt_out-1).

Turbines in Board-certificated wind farms must be at least 1.1 times total height from the wind farm property line and at least 1,125 feet from the blade tip to the nearest adjacent property line, unless all adjacent owners waive it.
